item.title: Nepal, UNDP launch $49.94 million project to reduce glacial lake flood risks
item.description: The Nepali government and the United Nations Development Programme (UNDP) have launched the USD 49.94 million GLOF-Sanjibani Project to protect Himalayan communities from glacial lake outburst floods.
item.content:encoded:
Nepal, UNDP launch $49.94 million project to reduce glacial lake flood risks The Nepali government and the United Nations Development Programme (UNDP) have launched the USD 49.94 million GLOF-Sanjibani Project to protect Himalayan communities from glacial lake outburst floods. Running from 2026 to 2033, the initiative will lower water levels in four high-altitude glacial lakes, strengthen early warning systems, and build protective downstream infrastructure. ANI | Updated: 26-11-2026 18:29 IST | Created: 26-11-2026 18:29 IST

Representative Image (File Photo/Reuters). Image Credit: ANI

SHARE

Key Takeaways AI Summary

Analyzing article...

In partnership with the United Nations Development Programme (UNDP), the Nepali government has rolled out a multimillion-dollar initiative aimed at safeguarding vulnerable Himalayan communities against glacial lake outburst floods (GLOFs). Unveiled in Nepal on Wednesday, the GLOF-Sanjibani Project seeks to mitigate hazards stemming from glacial lake outbursts by reducing water levels in high-altitude glacial lakes, bolstering early warning systems and constructing protective infrastructure in downstream regions, the UNDP said in a statement. Valued at USD 49.94 million, the initiative is scheduled to run from 2026 through 2033. According to the UNDP, a core goal of the programme involves lowering water levels in four high-altitude glacial lakes: Dona, Lumding Tsho and Lower Barun by three metres each, and Hongu 2 by one metre. "Beyond lake lowering, the project will strengthen climate-risk information and planning, expand hydrological and meteorological monitoring, and establish and improve early warning systems. It will also introduce nature-based solutions and protective infrastructure to reduce downstream flood risks in the watersheds," the statement read. The initiative follows catastrophic floods that hit Nepal on August 26, claiming over 1,400 lives while leaving more than 5,000 individuals, including foreign nationals, unaccounted for. The calamity also inflicted widespread destruction on both public and private infrastructure and swept away numerous settlements along the Bhotekoshi and Trishuli river corridors. Over recent years, climbing temperatures have accelerated glacier melt across the Himalayas, heightening fears of glacial lake instability, avalanches and potentially devastating downstream flooding. Funding for the endeavour comprises a USD 36.16 million grant from the Green Climate Fund, alongside USD 11.32 million in co-financing from the Nepali government, USD 2.14 million from the UNDP and USD 0.32 million contributed by private-sector partners. The UNDP said the project is projected to directly benefit over 385,000 people, 55 per cent of whom are women, while offering indirect protection to nearly two million more residents inhabiting downstream river basins. Previously, Nepal had reduced water levels at Tsho Rolpa in Dolakha district and Imja Lake in Solukhumbu district to curb the threat of glacial lake outburst floods. (ANI)

item.title: Trump wishes Robert Pattinson ‘luck’ as new James Bond, recalls 2012 tweet on star’s ex Kristen Stewart
item.description: When asked about Pattinson, Trump asked an aide to bring him articles about the actor before sharing his views. He also asked whether the new James Bond was a conservative ...
item.content:encoded:
Trump wishes Robert Pattinson ‘luck’ as new James Bond, recalls 2012 tweet on star’s ex Kristen Stewart When asked about Pattinson, Trump asked an aide to bring him articles about the actor before sharing his views. He also asked whether the new James Bond was a conservative ANI | Updated: 26-11-2026 17:09 IST | Created: 26-11-2026 17:09 IST

Donald Trump (L) James Bond poster (R) (Photos/instagram/Reuters/007). Image Credit: ANI

SHARE

Key Takeaways AI Summary

Analyzing article...

US President Donald Trump has wished actor Robert Pattinson good luck after his casting as the new James Bond. According to The New York Post, during an interaction with reporters at the Oval Office on Tuesday, Trump also recalled his 2012 tweet about Pattinson’s relationship with actor Kristen Stewart. When asked about Pattinson, Trump asked an aide to bring him articles about the actor before sharing his views. He also asked whether the new James Bond was a conservative before going through the printed articles brought to him by his aide Natalie Harper, as per The New York Post. “Is James Bond conservative? Natalie,” he called through the open door of the Oval Office. Looking at the reports, Trump said, “I always like people that like me.” As per the publication, one of the articles included his old tweet from 2012, in which he had commented on Pattinson and Stewart’s relationship after reports of Stewart cheating on the actor. Reading his post aloud, Trump, as per the publication, said, “Robert Pattinson should not take back Kristen Stewart. She cheated on him like a dog & will do it again, just watch.” He then added, “This was a long time ago.” At the time, Pattinson and Stewart, who played the lead roles in the ‘Twilight’ film series, were dating, as per The New York Post. Their relationship came under public attention after Stewart was photographed with filmmaker Rupert Sanders. Trump, who was then a reality television star, had shared several posts about the couple on social media in 2012. He continued commenting on their relationship even after they briefly got back together before eventually parting ways. Pattinson was named the new James Bond last week, making him the seventh actor to take on the role of the iconic British spy. Pattinson's announcement as the next James Bond brought an end to months of speculation surrounding the actor who would take over the iconic role. Several names had reportedly been in consideration, including Callum Turner, Jack Lowden, Nicholas Hoult, Josh O'Connor, Tom Francis, Aaron Taylor-Johnson, Harris Dickinson and Harry Styles, according to Variety. After going through the articles about the actor, Trump also reacted to some of the reports that included positive comments about him. “That’s cute. He says nice things,” Trump said. (ANI)

item.title: Networking, communications to dominate India's semiconductor market with 33.3% share by 2030: CareEdge
item.description: Networking and communications is projected to emerge as the largest segment of India's semiconductor market by 2030, according to a report by CareEdge Advisory.
item.content:encoded:
Networking, communications to dominate India's semiconductor market with 33.3% share by 2030: CareEdge Networking and communications is projected to emerge as the largest segment of India's semiconductor market by 2030, according to a report by CareEdge Advisory. ANI | Updated: 26-11-2026 16:03 IST | Created: 26-11-2026 16:03 IST

Representative Image (Photo/Reuters). Image Credit: ANI

SHARE

Key Takeaways AI Summary

Analyzing article...

Networking and communications is projected to emerge as the largest segment of India's semiconductor market by 2030, according to a report by CareEdge Advisory. The report noted that India's semiconductor demand is gradually shifting from traditional consumer electronics towards connectivity and computing applications. "The demand mix is increasingly shifting towards connectivity and computing applications," the report said. The share of networking and communications in semiconductor revenues is projected to increase from 26.1 per cent in 2020 to 33.3 per cent by 2030, with the segment registering a compound annual growth rate (CAGR) of 17.8 per cent. This growth will be supported by rising semiconductor demand from 5G deployment, network modernisation, fibre infrastructure expansion and increasing data traffic, as per the report. “Networking & Communications and Computing & Data Storage together are estimated to account for over 50.0% of semiconductor revenue by CY30,” it said. As per the report, the share of the computing and data storage segment is expected to increase from 12.8 per cent to 15.1 per cent during the same period, with the segment growing at a CAGR of 11.9 per cent. In contrast, the share of consumer electronics is projected to decline from 29.1 per cent to 22.2 per cent, reflecting the growing contribution of digital infrastructure, cloud computing and artificial intelligence (AI)-led demand. Overall, India's semiconductor market is projected to more than double from USD 45-50 billion in 2026 to USD 100-110 billion by 2030. However, limited domestic manufacturing capacity continues to drive India's dependence on semiconductor imports. "India’s semiconductor imports more than tripled from USD 11.9 billion in FY21 to USD 36.5 billion in FY26," the report said, highlighting that "imports account for 90–95% of domestic demand for semiconductor devices and components." To strengthen domestic manufacturing capabilities, 12 semiconductor projects involving cumulative investments exceeding Rs 1.64 lakh crore have been approved under the India Semiconductor Mission across six states. Of these, five projects had commenced commercial production by October 2026. The next phase of the mission is expected to strengthen capabilities in research and development, materials, equipment and talent development. The report further noted that while India has established expertise in chip design and related services, wafer fabrication remains at an early stage, with limited domestic capabilities in semiconductor materials and manufacturing equipment. "Timely project execution, manufacturing yields, technology partnerships, specialised talent and supplier development will be essential to improving domestic value addition and strengthening supply-chain resilience," the report said. (ANI)

item.title: Trump touts Iran naval blockade and "one-day win" in Venezuela while slamming reporter over coverage
item.description: In a post on his Truth Social platform, Trump sang praises of his administration's achievements, citing the closing of the border, crime stats, and tax and regulation cuts among others.
item.content:encoded:
Trump touts Iran naval blockade and "one-day win" in Venezuela while slamming reporter over coverage In a post on his Truth Social platform, Trump sang praises of his administration's achievements, citing the closing of the border, crime stats, and tax and regulation cuts among others.  ANI | Updated: 26-11-2026 14:04 IST | Created: 26-11-2026 14:04 IST

US President Donald Trump (Photo/Reuters). Image Credit: ANI

SHARE

Key Takeaways AI Summary

Analyzing article...

US President Donald Trump on Thursday (local time) slammed New York Times correspondent David E. Sanger for omitting what he described as key administrative achievements from his recent report, calling him a "mediocre reporter" who "only writes what he is told to write by his bosses". In a post on his Truth Social platform, Trump sang praises of his administration's achievements, citing the closing of the border, crime stats, and tax and regulation cuts among others. Mentioning two of his latest military operations: Iran and Venezuela, the US President highlighted "the most successful naval blockade" amid the ongoing conflict with Iran while reiterating his claims of annihilating the Iranian navy and air force "and more!" and his "ONE DAY WIN" against Venezuela. "David E. Sanger, the mediocre reporter for the Failing New York Times, didn’t mention in his recent story on me the successful closing of the Border, best crime stats in years (lowest murder rate since 1900 - 126 years!), biggest Tax and Regulation Cuts, EVER, the most successful naval blockade in history, the destruction of Iran’s Navy and Air Force (and more!), the ONE DAY WIN against Venezuela," he wrote. Further hailing the recent controlled detonation of nearly five tonnes of unstable lead azide at the Iowa Army Ammunition Plant, Trump wrote, " and today’s big success in straightening out the Obama-caused mess in Iowa." Trump also noted market performance "until the election" and his claim of settling 8 wars to slam the journalist for failing to cover the administration's contribution in boosting the pride of the country. "David Sanger is a lowlife that only writes what he is told to write by his bosses. Also, until the Election, best Market, EVER, 82 days, settled 8 Wars, and the USA is respected again like never before!" Trump asserted. Trump's post reflects his continued criticism of mainstream media outlets and their reporting on foreign policy and national security matters, particularly regarding Iran Earlier in May, Trump lashed out at several US media outlets, particularly The New York Times, The Wall Street Journal, and CNN, over their coverage of the ongoing situation with Iran, accusing them of misrepresenting Tehran's military position amid the escalating situation. In a post on Truth Social, Trump wrote that even if Iran were to surrender completely, its navy and air force destroyed, military leadership capitulating, and necessary surrender documents signed, the media would still portray the country as achieving a "masterful and brilliant victory over the United States". The US President also slammed the Democrats in the US and criticised the faction media as well as his political rivals, claiming that "They have gone absolutely CRAZY." "If Iran surrenders, admits their Navy is gone and resting at the bottom of the sea, and their Air Force is no longer with us, and if their entire Military walks out of Tehran, weapons dropped and hands held high, each shouting "I surrender, I surrender" while wildly waving the representative White Flag, and if their entire remaining Leadership signs all necessary "Documents of Surrender," and admit their defeat to the great power and force of the magnificent U.S.A., The Failing New York Times, The China Street Journal (WSJ!), Corrupt and now Irrelevant CNN, and all other members of the Fake News Media, will headline that Iran had a Masterful and Brilliant Victory over The United States of America, it wasn't even close," Trump had written. Meanwhile, tensions in West Asia continue, with reports indicating that Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu has urged the US administration to consider renewed military action against Tehran. (ANI)
